title.narrative: Output 1.3. Indonesia: Komnas HAM (the NHRI) has strengthened its capacity for promoting integrated implementation of human rights and SDGs and collaborate with relevant state actors for integrated implementation of human rights and SDGs.

Training of Komnas HAM staff; preliminary mapping of complaints against SDG goals and targets; published policy brief; Documented interaction between Komnas HAM, the SDG Secretariat of the Ministry of National Development Planning (BAPPENAS), the National Bureau of Statistics, and the Ministry of Law and Human Rights (at least 3 workshops or dialogues); Komnas HAM communications to regional SDG working group (at least 2).

target.value: Komnas HAM engages in dialogues with relevant ministries and other national actors to bring a human rights perspective to SDG implementation, monitoring and reporting. Experimental integration of artificial intelligence toolkit into complaints handling system to facilitate processing and analysis, including with regard to the SDGs. Komnas HAM actively engages with and where possible leads regional NHRI engagement with SDG processes with technical assistance from the Institute.

actual.value: 2 studies on Komnas HAM’s (the NHRI) role in relation to SDG processes in Indonesia and on how their work on Covid-19 and human rights is relevant for national planning were finalized and presented to stakeholders. Dialogue was conducted with staff from the Ministry for Political, Legal, and Security Affairs and the Ministry of National Development Planning. Staff from both Ministries now support the involvement of Komnas HAM in national SDG processes, policy and programme development.

target.value: The project agreement and result framework is put in place.
Capacity building of key staff of Komnas HAM on the SDGs and human rights. Scoping process by Komnas HAM analysing options for strategic engagement in SDG-processes in Indonesia.

actual.value: Activity planning for 2020 with Komnas HAM (the NHRI) in Indonesia was largely delayed due to Covid-19. Nevertheless, DIHR managed to establish good liaison with the NHRI during a webinar on Human Rights, Covid-19 and the SDGs (not funded by the project), where DIHR served as a speaking contributor. Two studies were set in motion towards the end of 2020 and will be finalised in 2021. One study focuses on Komnas HAM’s general role in relation to SDG processes in Indonesia and aims at identifying the main convergence between Komnas HAM’s work and advocacy, and the 2030 Agenda, with a view to build a stronger and more sustained strategic engagement in relevant processes. The other study focuses on linking Komnas HAM’s work on Covid-19 and human rights to the 2030 Agenda and the SDGs, again with a view to underpin strategic planning around further work in this area.

target.value: Best practices for integrated implementation are documented and experiences are shared at regional and global levels.

actual.value: Other activities included a series of capacity-building webinars for staff; production of a regional report on experiences from other NHRIs working with SDG issues and processes; and production of an addendum to Komnas HAM’s Annual Report on human rights issues documented and recommendations from an SDG lens. Komnas Ham’s Strategic Plan now includes an element on Sustainable Development and the SDGs. The target concerning use of the algorithm was dropped for technical reasons and language barriers.

title.narrative: Output 1.1. Honduras: Relevant state actors have strengthened capacity and collaboration for integrated implementation of human rights and the SDGs.

Capacity-strengthening activities conducted with the Secretaría de Coordinación General de Gobierno (SCGG), National Institute for Human Rights (CONADEH), Ministry of Human Rights (SEDH), National Bureau of Statistics, civil society networks.

target.value: The project agreement and result framework is put in place.

Potential for integrated implementation and reporting is mapped through alignment of international obligations in the areas of human rights and sustainable development, SCGG, the Ministry of Human Rights and the national and subnational branches of CONADEH explore opportunities to improved human rights delivery and protection through a coordinated approach with the development sector.

actual.value: Collaborative study on the impact of COVID-19 to the realization of the SDGs initiated in partnership with the NHRI (CONADEH), Ministry of Human Rights (SEDH), OHCHR and the European Union (ProDerechos Project). The study was expected to be finalized in December 2020 but it has been delayed due to the two hurricanes which hit and devastated the infrastructure in Honduras in November/December. It is now expected to be finished in the first quarter of 2021.

target.value: Digitalization of database and development of an online portal for the NHRI recommendations, linked to the SDGs. Capacity building modules and training for the NHRI staff on the integrated approach to SDGs and human rights.

actual.value: DIHR contributed to improving CONADEH’s systems to facilitate access to and follow-up of human rights recommendations. The online portal for the recommendations system is near completion. DIHR also developed training material to the staff of CONADEH on the 2030 Agenda. The materials will serve to build the capacity the CONADEH staff.

target.value: Collaborative study on the impact of COVID-19 to the realization of the SDGs, from a human rights perspective. Experimental integration of artificial intelligence toolkit into complaints handling system to facilitate processing and analysis including with regard to the SDGs.

actual.value: The collaborative study was carried out in partnership with the National Human Rights Commission (CONADEH), the Ministry of Human Rights, a local think-thank, UN and EU partners. Through the process, CONADEH strengthened its collaboration with public authorities, CSOs and international human rights bodies. The process of using the SDG algorithm into the NHRI complaints handling system to facilitate analysis of their data was nearly completed in the project timeframe).e future.

title.narrative: Documentation of institutionalised steps towards integrated implementation and monitoring of human rights and the 2030 Agenda in Honduras, Indonesia and Kenya.

target.value: Relevant state institutions in Honduras, Indonesia and Kenya apply human rights standards and recommendations in their SDG implementation and monitoring, including through cooperation with their NHRIs.

actual.value: Documented uptake of tools and analysis and institutionalised steps towards integrated implementation and monitoring of human rights’ and the 2030 Agenda in Kenya, Indonesia, Honduras including through cooperation with NHRIs.

title.narrative: Output 1.2. Kenya: Relevant tools and analysis are developed, and capacity building and dialogue have taken place to facilitate improved coordination and collaboration between key state actors on a human rights-based approach to sustainable development.

Context-specific analysis and tools are available and used by key state and other actors, capacity is built among key state actors, and dialogue and joint activities between the KNCHR and state actors informed by the KNCHR’s data and analysis have been initiated; a policy paper on a HRBA to implementation of the current development plan is published; at least one training has taken place with targeted state and other actors; complaints to the KNCHR have been categorized and analysed through and SDG lens; at least one concrete direct collaboration between state actor(s) and the KNCHR has been established; and KNCHR has produced at least two monitoring reports that integrate an SDG lens to the recommendations provided to the State.

target.value: KNCHR has integrated an SDG lens in its methodologies and tools for monitoring and follow-up to human rights recommendations in Kenya. SDG-human rights reporting for two key KNCHR reports (one national and one international) has been undertaken and follow up to recommendations is being undertaken. Best practices for integrated implementation are documented and experiences are shared at regional and global levels.

actual.value: A national workshop on data on persons with disabilities drew participants from KNBS and KNCHR as well as a number of state institutions, UN agencies, national and international NGOs. Participants reviewed the national survey on support needs for persons with disabilities and built capacity of technical focal points on a HRBA to data collection. It resulted in a revised methodology, which has now been piloted. KNCHR has developed its own SDG strategy and now has an SDG focal point. Experiences have been documented and shared.

target.value: Specific joint activities have been undertaken by KNCHR with relevant state actors with a view to enhancing a HRBA to data. Direct collaboration between KNCHR and key state actors on a human rights-based approach to SDG implementation and monitoring is informing key strategic areas of SDG implementation.

actual.value: Joint activities undertaken, incl. a training and national stakeholder dialogue on a HRBA to SDG data was organized by DIHR and KNCHR in collaboration the KNBS with participation from the State Department for Planning, the OHCHR and the Kenya SDGs Forum (CSO coalition). The workshop led to the inclusion of KNCHR in key official data initiatives and working groups. It also led to agreement to collaborate with the KNBS on data collection on vulnerable groups.

target.value: Strategic entry points for the promotion of a human rights-based approach in the implementation of Kenya’s current Medium-Term Development Plan III have been identified through a scoping exercise and development of a policy paper and engagement plan have been finalized. Key state actors have been trained on HRBA to SDGs and are being engaged regularly by KNCHR. KNCHR’s existing databases of complaints and other human rights information is categorised and used to produce analysis to feed into SDG-related policy work.

actual.value: Postponed to 2021 due the heavy workload of the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNHRC) in monitoring human rights issues related to Covid-19 in Kenya.

target.value: The project agreement and result framework is put in place by the end of the year.

actual.value: The project agreement was signed and the result framework was put in place.
